why: The statement asks only for infinitude for every admissible a, so the OpenAI theorem (c_a x/(log x)^2 primes in (x,2x) for every non-square a != -1) is whole in scope; it is unreviewed (VibeMathed is a catalogue, Persiflage explicitly did not verify, Lean chain has a sorry) and doubtful rather than not_credible because it is days old and the doubt is specific but not an identified error: its Theorem 1.2 would give a uniform zero-free strip for all Dirichlet L-functions, a result far beyond known technology. AI role is generated from the lab README with no human author. GRH- or conjecture-conditional results (Hooley, Fan-Pollack, Goldmakher et al., Perucca-Shparlinski, Murty-Naik) are reductions to unproved hypotheses and score none; average-over-a, function-field, number-field, two-variable and monoid results are variants. Heath-Brown's 'all but at most two a' is a case. Carella's claims score whole/case but not_credible on multiple F10 signals (eight years of silence on a landmark claim, scope ballooning across 14 revisions, later work still calling it open, no answer to the GRH barrier). The two companion manuscripts are an input lemma (none) and a zero-free-region result for a different question (variant).
doubts: openai-math-029 and openai-2026-10-primitive-roots-all-bases describe the same manuscript (029 also bundles the conditional simultaneous-bases paper); they are answered identically. The record does not confirm the README's 'vast majority' sentence covers this specific manuscript, though no human author is named and it is not among the named exceptions. Carella's progressions paper is unclear on whether q = 1 is included; judged whole but set aside as not_credible either way. Gupta-Murty could be read as a case; judged none since it settles no specific a.
